This testimonial emphasizes openness and self-correction, which typically nudges the openness/integrity subscales of trust more than overall behavior. I'd estimate the multidimensional trust effect around +3 points, with the single-item post-treatment measure likely showing a smaller, moderate shift given pre-treatment anchoring.

I'll set distrust to decrease modestly and funding perceptions, institutional trust, and communication-related outcomes to move slightly positive too. Since the piece also stresses uncertainty rather than pushing a strong message, belief and concern outcomes should shift only slightly, with policy support, behavioral intentions, and incentivized measures like donations or signups showing only marginal gains — net positive overall, driven mainly by the integrity/openness framing outweighing any competence-signaling tradeoff from admitting uncertainty.
